Setting up a qPCR run 1.Thaw qPCR reagents and samples on ice and briefly spin down before starting. 2. steps.title: Sample Pre-processing and Viral Enrichment
steps.instruction: Prepare environmental samples for virus concentration based on sample type.

substeps.instruction: For poultry drinking water or wetland surface water: Transfer 200 mL into sterile 200 mL polypropylene centrifuge tubes.
For wetland pond sediment: Add 5 g of sediment to 100 mL of autoclaved Milli-Q water in sterile centrifuge tubes.
For bird's cage swabs: Transfer the swab into a sterile centrifuge tube containing 50 mL of PBS (squeeze EDC using a sterile spatula to recover maximum PBS volume).
Vortex all samples thoroughly to ensure proper mixing.
Store re-suspended samples at -80°C until further use.

steps.title: Virus Concentration via PEG Precipitation
steps.instruction: Concentrate virus particles from the pre-processed environmental samples.

substeps.instruction: Incubate the mixture at 4°C for 2 hours under static or shaking conditions.
Centrifuge the tubes at 12,000 rpm for 90 minutes at 4°C.
Carefully decant the supernatant and remove any remaining liquid without dislodging the pellet.
Re-suspend the pellet in 1 mL of nuclease-free water and vortex briefly.
Centrifuge the samples at 8,000 rpm for 20 minutes to remove solid debris.
Carefully transfer the clear supernatant to new sterile centrifuge tubes (100 mL or 200 mL, depending on original volume).
Add 10% (w/v) PEG 8000 and 5.58% NaCl to the collected supernatant.
Vigorously mix by shaking or inverting the tube until PEG and NaCl are completely dissolved.

steps.title: RNA Isolation using Trizol and QIAamp Kit
steps.instruction: Extract viral RNA from the concentrated sample using a combined Trizol and column-based method.

substeps.instruction: Aliquot 200 µL of the sample from the PEG concentration step and add 1 mL of Trizol reagent; vortex thoroughly and incubate at room temperature for 5 minutes.
Add 200 µL of chloroform, vortex briefly, and incubate at room temperature for 5 minutes.
Centrifuge at 12,000 x g for 15 minutes at 4°C.
Transfer the aqueous phase to a fresh RNAse-free micro-centrifuge tube.
Add an equal volume of ethanol (96-100%) to the aqueous phase, pulse-vortex for 15 seconds, and briefly centrifuge to remove lid droplets.
Transfer 600 μL of the solution to a QIAamp Mini column (in a 2 mL collection tube), centrifuge at 6,000 x g (8,000 rpm) for 1 min, and discard the flow-through.
Repeat the transfer and centrifugation for the remaining solution, then discard the flow-through.
Add 500 μL of buffer AW1 to the column, centrifuge at 6,000 x g (8,000 rpm) for 1 minute, and discard the flow-through.
Add 500 μL of Buffer AW2 to the column and centrifuge at full speed (20,000 x g; 14,000 rpm) for 3 minutes.
Centrifuge again at full speed (20,000 x g; 14,000 rpm) for 1 minute to remove residual Buffer AW2.
Place the column in a clean 1.5 mL micro-centrifuge tube, add 40 μL of room-temperature Buffer AVE, and incubate at room temperature for 1 min.
Centrifuge at 6,000 x g (8,000 rpm) for 1 minute and store the elute at -20°C.

steps.title: RNA Isolation from VTM Samples
steps.instruction: Isolate total nucleic acid from poultry litter, bird droppings, molted feathers, and air samples using the MagMAX Viral/Pathogen Nucleic Acid Isolation Kit and KingFisher Flex processor.

substeps.instruction: Set up the KingFisher Flex Magnetic Particle Processor with 96 Deep-Well Head and Heating Block, and load the MVP_2Wash_200_Flex program.
Prepare processing plates and cover with MicroAmp Clear Adhesive Film; store at room temperature for up to 1 hour.
Thaw VTMs used for air sampling at 37°C if solidified.
Prepare Binding Bead Mix: Vortex Total Nucleic Acid Magnetic Beads and mix according to the kit table; store at room temperature.
Prepare the sample plate: Add 5 µL of Proteinase K to each sample well, 200 µL of sample to each sample well, and 200 µL of Nuclease-free Water to the Negative Control well.
Invert Binding Bead Mix 5 times and add 275 µL to each sample and negative control well.
Add 200 μL of sample collected in VTM (Note: pipet Binding Bead Mix slowly and use fresh tips for each well).
Run the MVP_2Wash_200_Flex program on the KingFisher Flex, loading plates when prompted.
Immediately remove the Elution Plate after the run (~22 minutes) and seal with MicroAmp Clear Adhesive Film to prevent evaporation.

steps.title: Digital PCR Setup and Run
steps.instruction: Perform digital PCR to detect and quantify Influenza A Virus (IAV) RNA.

substeps.instruction: Aliquot 7 µL of prepared master-mix into 0.2 mL 96-well PCR plates or tubes.
Add templates, negative controls, and positive controls to the assigned wells.
Seal plates/tubes with adhesive seals/caps and briefly spin down to remove bubbles.
Gently transfer the reaction mix from PCR plates/strips to nanoplate wells without creating bubbles.
Seal nanoplate wells with the provided rubber adhesive seal (do not centrifuge the nanoplate).
Set thermal cycling and imaging parameters in the digital PCR system, insert the nanoplate, and start the protocol.

steps.title: Data Collection and Analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze digital PCR results to determine copy numbers of targeted RNA.

substeps.instruction: Adjust the threshold line using auto-thresholding or manually to separate negative and positive partitions.
Save results and remove the plate from the instrument.
Calculate total copy numbers using the formula: [(Total PCR reaction volume in µL / volume of RNA template in µL used in PCR reaction) x (obtained copy numbers/µL)].
Example calculation: (12 µL PCR reaction volume / 5 µL RNA template) x (obtained copy numbers/µL).
